comment:
The manual says Loop 'derives BPM information when it is present in the file or filename'. The code looks at the filename only: Loop.cpp:176-187 scans the name for the letters bpm and reads the digits immediately before them. No chunk inside the WAV is parsed. The bar count is then derived from that tempo and the file length, and only accepted when it lands within 15% of a whole number of bars (Loop.cpp:189-198).

The manual says 'Bar Shift moves the playback window by bars'. Loop.cpp:426 divides the whole file into eight equal steps regardless of the Bars setting, so the shift is in eighths of the file, which only equals a bar when Bars is 8.

The Bars CV clamps the total to a minimum of 1 (Loop.cpp:344), so a patched Bars CV can never reach the knob's own 0 position and the automatic length cannot be selected by voltage.

The Reverse CV inverts the switch rather than setting it (Loop.cpp:287-288): with the switch already on, holding the input above 1V plays the sample forwards.

The panel prints CLK beside the sync switch and beside the clock jack; the maker's tooltip for the switch is Sync. The switch comes up on (Loop.cpp:99).

The waveform display and the text on it are one custom widget with no parameter behind them, so nothing there can be clicked for help.
